item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Works by Fatyma Khan — Sun Aug 2, 12:00 AM — North York Central Library
item.description: Throughout the month of August, works by artist Fatyma Khan are on display at North York Central Library branch. Fatyma Khan is an award-winning abstract art photographer based in Toronto. Fatyma Khan's work delves into the intricate relationship between individuals and their environments, emphasizing textural composition and the evocative study of light. Fatyma’s photography is marked by a contemplative approach, capturing the emotional and psychological landscapes shaped by spatial context. Her images often reflect the subtle tension between inner experience and outward reality, offering viewers a space to engage with the layered complexities of perception, presence, and place. This exhibit is part of TPL's Art Exhibits Space program. Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city. item.title: TMDL + MCP + PBIP: desarrollo agéntico de modelos semánticos con Git y CI/CD — Mon Aug 3, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto En esta primera sesión de la serie “Power BI + MCP: la nueva forma de conectar IA con tus datos”, introduciremos Model Context Protocol (MCP) y explicaremos cómo puede utilizarse junto con Power BI para conectar herramientas de IA con datos empresariales confiables.
Los asistentes aprenderán qué es MCP, qué son los Power BI MCP Servers y cómo pueden ayudar a que las herramientas de IA interactúen con modelos semánticos de Power BI. Cubriremos los conceptos principales, casos de uso habituales, consideraciones de configuración y el valor de utilizar modelos semánticos como una capa de datos gobernada para experiencias de analítica con IA.
La sesión será práctica y orientada a desarrolladores, con ejemplos pensados para entender cómo MCP puede integrarse en flujos modernos de Power BI y analítica.
Source: Meetup: Microsoft Reactor Toronto

- A grasp of planning out fun game-play mechanics
- Familiarity with features of the Godot Game Engine

item.title: BOOK LAUNCH - GOING SOUTH: TRACING THE MASAI FROM THE MIDDLE EAST TO EAST AFRICA, BY PAUL KUNONI — Sat Aug 8, 5:00 PM — Blackhurst Cultural Centre
item.description:
Join scientific researcher Paul Kunoni for the launch of his newly published book, GOING SOUTH: TRACING THE MAASAI FROM THE MIDDLE EAST TO EAST AFRICA. What forces shaped the rise of the Maasai in East Africa, and how did one family's story become intertwined with the region's complex history of migration, colonization, and cultural survival?
Going South: Tracing the Maasai from the Middle East to East Africa by Paul Nkuo Kunoni traces the historical, cultural, and political pathways that shaped the Maasai people and their enduring legacy in the region. *GOING SOUTH will be available for purchase at the event. Look forward to remarks from the author, a live reading, Q&A and an opportunity to have your copy of the book signed by Paul. Admission: Free. All are welcome! Students and scholars especially of African history, political science, international relations and the like, will be interested in GOING SOUTH and Paul's talk. See you there!
Source: A Different Booklist

item.title: Virtual REGISTER: Little Caesar Classic Movie — Sat Aug 8, 7:15 PM
item.description:
Experience Toronto **Note: After you RSVP, you will also need to Register to receive your link to the event.**
On **Saturday, August 8th,** **see Little Caesar, a classic crime film.** A landmark of early gangster cinema, *Little Caesar* helped define the genre with its gritty atmosphere and unforgettable performance by Edward G. Robinson as the ruthless Rico Bandello. Released in 1931, the film captures the rise-and-fall intensity of Prohibition-era crime stories, with Robinson’s fierce, compact energy turning Rico into one of Hollywood’s first great gangster icons. For anyone who loves classic crime films, this is one of the big ones: lean, tough, and powered by the kind of performance that made Warner Bros. gangster pictures legendary.
